ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq.; Loi n° 2016-1691 (Sapin II); Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Décret n° 2020-118 of 11 February 2020 (French beneficial ownership register – RBE); Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-17; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; French RBE maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and integrated into the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access restricted to legitimate-interest verification following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 Sovim; French implementing measures require demonstration of legitimate interest; French AML obligated entities such as banks, notaries, and incorporation agents retain access for KYC/AML purposes)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each direct shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, consulate or sworn translator in the country of residence; original notarization required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the 1961 Convention; Consular Legalization at French Embassy for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and extract of Directors/Register of Members of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or Registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague states, double legalization via Ministry of Foreign Affairs and French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) granted to local incorporation counsel or agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly authorized signatory of the corporate shareholder, notarized where required by the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or commercial address of UBOs and proposed directors (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certification by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) where issued in a foreign language; notarization and apostille only if the registry contests authenticity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds clearance confirmation for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or financial institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled (Hague) or consular legalization for jurisdictions requiring it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, French Treasury asset-freezing orders (arrêtés de gel des avoirs), OFAC SDN List, and national PEP registers; obligations derive from CMF Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 aligning with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22; heightened due diligence applies to medium-risk digital advertising and performance media buying activity with cross-border payment rails (ACH, SWIFT/Wise); TRACFIN declaration required for any suspicious transaction or identity doubt; ongoing monitoring for the duration of the corporate relationship

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités Entreprises operated by INPI at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability search via INPI Data at https://data.inpi.fr and via the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) company database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination sociale) may be composed in any language provided it is transcribed in Latin characters; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated for RCS/RNE registration; the statutory suffix Société par Actions Simplifiée or the abbreviation SAS must appear on all corporate documents and in the legal announcement; the name must not be deceptive, contrary to public order, or create confusion with a prior trademark or corporate name
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: FRANCE / RÉPUBLIQUE (when implying State sponsorship or public concession)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI name reservation or the registration filing is refused, the applicant receives written grounds; the applicant may immediately refile with an amended denomation via the Guichet Unique; administrative recourse against INPI refusal may be raised with the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle; if the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce refuses RCS registration, judicial summary recourse (référé) lies before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce or Tribunal Judiciaire within 15 days under Article L.123-5 of the Code de commerce; the 120-day INPI reservation is non-renewable, and on expiry priority reverts to the first subsequent filer

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry; a French SAS may contractually domiciliate its registered office (siège social) with a licensed commercial domiciliation provider under Article L.123-11-1 of the Code de commerce; the provider must maintain real premises in France, offer mail receipt and forwarding services, and the address must be genuine, non-fictitious, and capable of receiving legal process; the digital advertising and affiliate media buying sector does not require a physical operational headquarters in France
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% within the first 36 months of operations; Greffiers and registry compliance officers may conduct unannounced domiciliation verification visits; tax authorities may carry out documentary substance reviews and, where abuse indicators exist, court-authorized search and seizure visits under Article L.16B of the Livre des procédures fiscales

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II – Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general company provisions of Articles L. 210-1 et seq.; implementing Decree No. 2022-1297 on the digital single filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and accessed through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société and supporting dossier filed electronically through the INPI Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital applies to an SAS. The articles of association fix the share capital. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed; at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the balance payable according to the articles (maximum five years). Funds are deposited in a blocked bank account, with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or with a notary until the RCS registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The form of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) and draft articles of association submitted are approved; the share capital of €1,000 is fully subscribed by the shareholders listed in the annex. 2. The President, [Full Name], is appointed for an unlimited term with full powers to manage the company, subject to law and articles. 3. The registered office is fixed at [Address] ([Insert legal representative option]). 4. The President is authorized to complete all registration filings, publish the required legal announcement, open bank accounts, and take all measures necessary to obtain the RCS extract, including making any capital deposit. 5. These resolutions are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve statutory drafts and execute the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel, notary optional, and all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders must finalize the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital amount, share class rights, President appointment, and internal governance rules. The articles must be drafted in French and executed by all shareholders or their authorized proxies.
required_dossiers: Valid identification document of each shareholder
Proof of physical or legal address of each shareholder
Power of attorney if the articles are signed by proxy
Draft articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary queries the draft, amend and re-execute the relevant provisions. If the corporate name is refused, conduct a fresh name availability check and re-submit an amended name clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal formation notice in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) approved for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory legal announcement (renseignements de constitution) to an authorized legal advertising journal. The notice must contain the registered office address, corporate purpose, share capital, trade name, and appointment details. Obtain the attestation de parution.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement
Final draft of the articles of association
Proof of registered office address or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, instruct the journal to expedite and issue a revised attestation. If the announcement contains errors, publish a corrective notice and obtain a corrected publication certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate capital deposit account and obtain the certificate of funds deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company bank account and arrange for each cash subscriber to transfer the subscribed cash contribution. The bank or notary must block the funds until the company is registered and then issue the attestation de dépôt de fonds. For contributions in kind, the contribution valuation report must be annexed to the articles.
required_dossiers: Subscriber list and subscription amounts
Individual identification documents of subscribers
Draft articles of association
Bank account opening form and KYC statement
Contribution valuation report if there are in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening, apply at another licensed credit institution or use a notary's escrow account. Re-issue the certificate once all contributions are properly received and blocked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete all formalities on the Guichet unique and upload the electronic supporting documents. The form will automatically collect the legal structure, registered office, object, directors, and beneficial owner information. The dossier must be certified by a representative who confirms the accuracy of the declarations.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of association
Attestation de parution from the legal announcements journal
Attestation de dépôt de fonds or notarial certificate
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Déclaration sur l'honneur de non-condamnation for legal representatives
Justificatif de domiciliation or occupancy title
Copy of identification document of each legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the pre-validation checklist identifies missing documents, correct the form and re-upload before final submission. The Guichet unique will indicate validation errors and allow an iterative cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the formation filing and pay registry taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete dossier electronically through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Pay the applicable state filing fees and any registry taxes online. The filing will be transmitted to the competent commercial court registry for review and registration in the RCS.
required_dossiers: Dossier assembled in Step 4
Confirmation of online payment of official fees
Power of attorney if a third-party agent submits the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a cause de rejet (rejection reason), the filer receives a detailed defect notice. Use the Guichet unique portal to amend, supplement, or replace the challenged documents within the cure period. If the rejection is considered erroneous, appeal through written correspondence to the registry and seek a formal review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the RCS registration extract (extrait Kbis) and SIRET number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal review, the registry registers the company and issues the extrait Kbis, which is the official identity certificate of the legal entity. Verify all legal and corporate data, including name, registered office, President, share capital, and ISIC/NAF code. Download the Kbis extract and retain it as proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: None; generated automatically by the registry after successful validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed or contains incorrect data, contact the registry through the Guichet unique with the dossier reference number and request correction or re-issuance. Legal counsel can expedite through the greffe's customer service if the statutory deadline is exceeded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish corporate governance records, share certificates, and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAS President and other corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a post-incorporation administrative set-up: issue share certificates to shareholders, open the securities register, create the minutes book, and ensure the registered address and officers are properly recorded. Deposit the Kbis with the operating bank and finalize employment or contractor agreements for business operations.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis from the RCS
Registered articles of association
Shareholder identity records
Corporate bank account opening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share certificates or register entries contain irregularities, amend the register with a rectification resolution and re-issue the certificates retroactively to the incorporation date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial or physical manufacturing installation is required for digital advertising, media arbitrage, and affiliate lead generation under ISIC 7310.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None; no regulated operational permits under the French ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) regime are triggered by an office-based performance media buying activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not required for pure digital service activity; no EIA filing, no ICPE authorization, and no environmental permit threshold is reached.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to industrial discharge or VOC emissions. The business must still comply with general waste disposal rules, including separate collection of electronic and office waste, and any HVAC emissions must comply with the local department prefect's health and safety orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must comply with the French Labor Code health and safety requirements for office premises. A fire safety certificate from the building owner or any applicable SDIS clearance is required for shared or tertiary buildings. Electrical installations must be verified in accordance with the Code du travail. If staff are employed, the company must register with the registered workplace health service (service de prévention et de santé au travail) and arrange periodic occupational health checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal – https://www.impots.gouv.fr/ (business registration via https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestic SAS obtains its SIREN/SIRET automatically from INSEE through the one-stop shop (Guichet unique) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and receives a French intra-community VAT number upon process completion. A non-resident entity must file Form Cerfa 15163 (or the foreign-operator procedure) with DGFiP, providing constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, director identification and powers of attorney, and, where required, appointing a fiscal representative ('représentant fiscal') responsible for French VAT and tax obligations. A provisional French TIN/VAT ID is issued within approximately 10 business days and a definitive VAT number is allocated after substance and activity verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists for the SAS; it is mandatorily subject to impôt sur les sociétés (IS). Available elective regimes include French tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') for groups, VAT grouping for fiscal unity, and participation-exemption elections for French Sociétés Mères. Hybrid mismatch provisions under the ATAD-inspired French tax law (LOI n° 2018-898) operate automatically and offer no elective mechanism for Article 239 quater transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA) under Code Général des Impôts, art. 256 et seq.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For domestic established businesses: €85,000 for supply of goods and €37,500 for supply of services (franchise en base thresholds) — exceeding either threshold triggers mandatory VAT registration. For non-established foreign suppliers, no minimum threshold applies; any taxable supply in France creates a VAT registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting under the French 2026 reform: all established taxable persons must issue and receive structured e-invoices through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) using EN 16931-compliant formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). Invoices must contain SIREN, SIRET, French VAT ID, a unique invoice identifier, and an electronic rating. Transaction data is transmitted near-real-time to DGFiP via secured APIs; there is no physical fiscal stamp requirement for standard exports, but customs export clearance in DELTA G / ECS (European Export Control System) must be completed digitally, and certain state or prepaid supplies require a prior digital authorization.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (effective 0% VAT) under CGI art. 262-I-1°, provided the goods leave France/EU by the seller or on its behalf, supported by customs export status and transport documents. For services (including affiliate media buying/brokerage) where the customer is a non-EU taxable person, the place of supply is outside France pursuant to CGI art. 259B, so no French VAT is chargeable; where the customer is EU VAT-registered, the B2B supply is zero-rated/reverse-charged in the customer's EU member state if a valid EU VAT ID is obtained. For services to non-taxable persons outside the EU, local consumption rules may still exempt French VAT if effectively used and enjoyed in the non-EU customer's country.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Déclaration d'exportation via DELTA G or ECS)
Bill of Lading (LTA/CMR/airway bill) evidencing transport out of France/EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificat de domiciliation devise / bank payment receipt)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under CGI art. 1727–1729 and Code des douanes art. 414, the export zero-rating can be retroactively clawed back where export documentation is fraudulent or the deadline is missed. DGFiP may issue rectification within the statutory six-year period (extended to ten years for concealed fraud). Penalties escalate from 10% (minor inaccuracy) to 40% (deliberate omission) and 80% for manœuvres frauduleuses, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%. Customs offences may incur criminal penalties up to three years’ imprisonment and a fine of two times the evaded VAT; the person claiming zero-rating is personally liable for restitution of VAT along with penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-exchange restrictions are principally governed by European Union law, French financial and monetary legislation, and anti-money-laundering rules administered and supervised by the relevant French authorities, including the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution and the Direction générale du Trésor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general French exchange-control regime requiring prior approval for ordinary commercial payments, dividend distributions, intercompany settlements, or foreign investment funding. Capital movements remain subject to sanctions compliance, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls, beneficial-owner verification, tax reporting, statistical reporting, and applicable French foreign-direct-investment screening. Outbound dividends and other profit remittances generally require properly approved corporate accounts, evidence of distributable profits, withholding-tax analysis, and completion of applicable tax formalities. Bank transfer delays may arise where the payment involves sanctioned countries, high-risk jurisdictions, complex ownership, unusual affiliate pricing, regulated advertising sectors, or insufficient evidence of the underlying transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to repatriate, surrender, or convert export proceeds within a prescribed period, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts may generally be retained in euro or foreign-currency accounts and converted at the company's discretion, subject to contractual bank terms, accounting requirements, sanctions controls, anti-money-laundering controls, and accurate tax and statistical reporting. Where payments relate to regulated goods, sanctioned counterparties, controlled jurisdictions, or documentary trade finance, additional evidence and reporting may be required. The company should maintain invoices, contracts, shipping or service-delivery evidence, customer and beneficial-owner information, and payment-reconciliation records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation, followed by EUR Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account where approved
Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation, followed by EUR Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account where approved

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional banking entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation, followed by EUR Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account where approved

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group banking entities, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne institutions
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation, followed by EUR Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account where approved
Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation, followed by EUR Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account where approved

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine EUR collections and payments, subject to provider eligibility and risk acceptance. A French SAS may use a European Union or European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution where the provider onboards French legal entities and provides the required account or payment services. Wise Business may be available for eligible French companies, but availability, account features, currencies, limits, and local receiving details must be confirmed directly with the provider. Mercury is a United States-focused financial-services platform and its availability to a French SAS, including ACH functionality, is not assured; ACH is a United States clearing rail and is not a substitute for SEPA. An EMI safeguarding account is not a bank deposit account and may not provide lending, deposit-guarantee protection, or all bank services. Offshore digital EMIs cannot lawfully be used to evade French or EU AML, sanctions, tax, beneficial-owner, payment-services, or transaction-reporting requirements. A regulated EMI may passport services within the EEA, but the precise service, local establishment, and supervisory status must be verified in the relevant regulator register.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted through qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents, and beneficial-owner verification. In practice, a bank may require a director, legal representative, ultimate beneficial owner, or authorized signatory to attend an in-person or live video interview, particularly for a newly incorporated SAS, foreign-owned structures, non-resident directors, complex affiliate relationships, high-volume media buying, unusual payment flows, or elevated geographic risk. Capital deposit accounts are subject to the onboarding policy of the chosen bank and normally require the incorporation file before the certificate of deposit is issued.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with no operating history, no French revenue, or a foreign parent and non-resident directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of registration or current Kbis extract; draft or executed articles of association; proof of registered office; shareholder and ultimate-beneficial-owner chart to natural persons; passports and address evidence for directors, signatories, and beneficial owners; board or shareholder resolutions authorizing account opening; business plan; first-year budget; expected transaction volumes; source-of-funds evidence; parent-company constitutional documents; and a clear explanation of the French operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital advertising media arbitrage, affiliate lead generation, or high-volume pass-through payments viewed as opaque or commercially unusual
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial-flow memorandum; advertiser, publisher, affiliate-network, and platform contracts; insertion orders; invoices; campaign reports; platform account ownership evidence; customer and supplier due-diligence policy; explanation of gross versus net revenue recognition; expected payment corridors; transaction-value bands; refund and chargeback controls; evidence that the company does not provide regulated financial, gambling, adult, healthcare, or other restricted advertising services without required approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High proportion of payments to or from related parties, offshore entities, or jurisdictions perceived as higher risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; beneficial-owner evidence for each counterparty; invoices and proof of service delivery; arm's-length pricing support; tax-residency certificates where relevant; sanctions and adverse-media screening records; written rationale for each payment corridor; and management approval thresholds for related-party transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth or source of funds cannot be reconciled to the proposed capital contribution or payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited financial statements; parent-company funding resolution; capital contribution agreement; loan agreement where applicable; sale-of-business or investment documents; tax filings or tax-residency evidence where appropriate; proof of prior business revenue; and a funds-flow diagram linking the originating account to the French SAS account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, pooled accounts, virtual IBANs, payment processors, or multiple fintech platforms without a documented treasury policy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal bank-account policy; approved account inventory; account ownership certificates; segregation-of-duties matrix; reconciliation procedures; payment-approval workflow; description of each payment processor's regulated status; prohibition on personal accounts; monthly bank reconciliations; and evidence that customer funds are not held or safeguarded as a regulated payment service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, or beneficial-owner screening alert
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution memorandum; certified identification documents; independent corporate-register extracts; ownership and control analysis; sanctions-screening results; explanation of any false positive; enhanced due-diligence report; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds package; and legal review before any transaction is released.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence tax residence, economic substance, or the purpose of cross-border affiliate payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-registration evidence; management and office arrangements; employee or contractor documentation where applicable; board minutes; service agreements; deliverables and campaign records; VAT analysis; withholding-tax analysis; transfer-pricing documentation; and a transaction-level reconciliation to the general ledger and tax returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment activity inconsistent with the stated business, including cryptocurrency exposure, cash activity, restricted-sector advertising, or unexplained third-party collections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-scope business statement; approved customer and supplier categories; prohibited-activity policy; transaction-monitoring rules; payment acceptance controls; third-party collection approvals; cryptocurrency prohibition or documented compliance framework; cash prohibition; and management certification that actual activity matches the onboarding profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Fund the SAS through a bank account or regulated payment account held in the SAS's legal name. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding from the Single Euro Payments Area and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies or banks. The remittance narrative should identify the transaction as share capital, share-premium funding, shareholder loan, or intercompany funding, as applicable; the legal characterization must match the corporate resolutions and accounting entries. For incorporation, deposit subscribed capital into a designated capital-deposit account and obtain the bank certificate required for registration. For post-incorporation funding, route funds to the operational account and retain the funding agreement, board or shareholder approval, source-of-funds evidence, and bank confirmation. Banks may request a purpose, invoice, contract, ownership chart, tax information, and proof of economic rationale before crediting or releasing funds. Do not split transfers to avoid monitoring thresholds, use third-party remitters without approval, or describe debt funding as equity. Reconcile the incoming transfer to the ledger and preserve the SWIFT or SEPA confirmation, value date, ordering customer, beneficiary, currency, and amount.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme and bank-supported limits. Use SWIFT cross-border payments for non-SEPA currencies, non-EEA counterparties, or banking corridors that require correspondent banking. A traditional SWIFT MT103 remains a payment-message reference for applicable bank processing, but banks are migrating to ISO 20022 formats, including pacs.008; the bank's current messaging standard should be confirmed. For documentary trade settlements, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or open-account payment according to the counterparty and risk profile. The bank may require a purchase order, commercial invoice, contract, transport or service-delivery evidence, beneficiary ownership information, sanctions screening, and approved purpose. For digital advertising and affiliate services, retain contracts, insertion orders, platform reports, invoices, proof of campaign delivery, and beneficiary-account verification. Ensure payment references are accurate, related-party payments are separately identified, and foreign-exchange conversion is performed by an authorized bank or regulated payment provider. Apply dual authorization, payment limits, beneficiary-change callbacks, sanctions screening, and independent bank-account verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards booked with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm for documented commercial exposures
Foreign-exchange swaps used for short-term liquidity and currency-risk management with an authorized counterparty
Currency options or option structures, subject to suitability, appropriateness, documentation, pricing, and product-governance requirements

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable or where settlement is conventionally cash-settled, subject to counterparty availability, local-market legality, and sanctions controls
Cross-currency swaps for material, documented multi-period exposures, subject to negotiated collateral, valuation, termination, and netting terms
Exchange-traded or centrally cleared currency derivatives where available and appropriate

Hedging arrangements must be linked to identifiable commercial, funding, or balance-sheet exposures and documented under appropriate master agreements, including ISDA documentation where relevant. EU EMIR obligations, including reporting, risk-mitigation, clearing, margin, and counterparty-classification requirements, may apply. Derivatives should not be used for unauthorized speculative activity, and accounting hedge documentation should be maintained where hedge accounting is intended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profits or losses by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS; decision recorded in the corporate minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court-authorised extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential director liability and court-ordered compliance; no general fixed filing fee applies to the approval itself.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and, where applicable, management report and auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) at the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registry or an interested party may seek a court order to file, potentially subject to a daily penalty. Failure to comply with an injunction may result in a fine; late filing can also expose the president to liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second working day following 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable electronic-filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and surcharges may apply; penalties depend on the delay, tax due, and circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if reportable information has changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), through the companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the company knows or should know of a change; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate, complete, and current information may result in criminal penalties for the responsible natural person and the company, and court-ordered compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor if it exceeds at least two of these thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate requirements may apply to groups, controlled companies, or specific regulated situations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French accounting standards (Plan comptable général) for statutory individual accounts; IFRS applies to consolidated accounts where required, including listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is generally required. File an update with the commercial court registry within 30 days after a change to reportable beneficial ownership information. Keep shareholder accounts, share-transfer records, and corporate minutes current; SAS records may be maintained electronically where legally valid.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholder accounts and share-transfer movement records
Corporate decision and shareholder meeting minutes
Register of beneficial owners information filed with the commercial court registry; no general requirement that it be kept on site

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 220-1,100 per year for commercial domiciliation, depending on provider and services; France does not generally require a separate registered-agent appointment.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,300-11,000 per year for a small-company statutory audit; actual fees depend on complexity and scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: French corporate income tax is generally 25%. Eligible small and medium-sized enterprises may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. A 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax may apply where corporate income tax exceeds EUR 763,000, producing a marginal combined rate of approximately 25.825%. No general corporate tax holiday applies to an ordinary digital advertising or affiliate media-buying SAS. Qualifying innovation, research and development, or specifically designated geographic incentives may apply only if statutory conditions are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats - impôt sur les sociétés), filed electronically through EDI-TDFC via an authorized intermediary or compatible accounting software. Tax payment and certain tax-account procedures use the impots.gouv.fr professional portal through the EFI system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return is generally due within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the usual deadline is the second business day following 1 May of the following year. Electronic payment installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with a final balance payment generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end, subject to the applicable filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, principal activity, fiscal year dates, and tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS is resident and files as a French corporate taxpayer. Foreign shareholders and parent entities are not substituted for the SAS identification details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable result and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss, taxable profit or loss, corporate income tax, tax credits, installments, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all profits attributable to the French SAS. Foreign-source income must be tested under applicable treaty and foreign-tax-credit rules; treaty relief does not remove the French filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow shareholder distributions, non-business expenses, unsupported management charges, and expenses lacking a direct business connection. Related-party charges require commercial evidence and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss utilization, carryforward, carryback, and remaining tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document losses separately by fiscal year. French loss utilization is subject to statutory annual limitations; losses are not automatically transferable to a foreign parent or affiliate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items affecting the taxable result and specific tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report relevant tax adjustments for provisions, capital gains, exempt dividends, tax credits, and other statutory items, with supporting schedules retained in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, depreciation, provisions, share capital, subsidiaries, participations, and related tax information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign subsidiaries, shareholder relationships, participations, and transactions with related non-resident entities. Apply treaty provisions only after verifying beneficial ownership and anti-abuse conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits, withholding taxes, and amounts already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require proof of foreign tax paid and must comply with the relevant treaty or French domestic limitation. Withholding tax suffered by foreign shareholders is not normally a credit of the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer-pricing summary declaration, where the statutory size or group conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material controlled transactions with foreign related parties, including advertising purchases, lead-generation fees, commissions, management services, financing, royalties, and year-end true-ups.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of certain general expenses, including specified management, entertainment, travel, and other potentially non-deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholder, director, and affiliate expenses must be separately supported by invoices, business purpose, beneficiary, and evidence of services received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credit and tax-reduction information, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the SAS and retain eligibility documentation, payroll data, research records, or other prescribed evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General ledger, trial balance, invoices, bank records, contracts, payroll records, intercompany statements, and statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Records must permit reconciliation of payments through Mercury, Wise, bank wires, card processors, and other payment rails to commercial contracts and invoices.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% where a formal notice remains unheeded and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent conduct or abusive concealment. Late payment generally attracts a 0.20% monthly interest charge, subject to statutory adjustments. Incorrect declarations may also trigger tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and criminal referral. Failure to file transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions lacking documentation, subject to applicable statutory limits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD for corporate income tax installments and balance, submitted and paid electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional EFI portal or through approved electronic accounting arrangements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally payable on the 15th day of March, June, September, and December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the fiscal year-end, with special rules for 31 December year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, tax account, fiscal year, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS tax account and SIREN. Do not use the foreign parent's tax identification number as the principal taxpayer identifier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax installment calculated by reference to prior-year or estimated current-year liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recalculate installments when the SAS has losses, tax credits, material related-party adjustments, or expected changes in taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between final annual liability and installments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065-SD and retain proof of payment and tax-account statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally results in 0.20% monthly interest and a 5% late-payment surcharge for tax debts, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments. Persistent non-payment may lead to formal collection, attachment of bank accounts, director or representative liability in exceptional circumstances, and criminal proceedings where fraudulent concealment is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% is the principal domestic withholding rate on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate recipient, subject to exemptions, treaty reductions, and specific recipient classifications. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may eliminate withholding where the qualifying ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A 12.8% domestic rate generally applies to certain individual recipients rather than non-resident corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, minimum participation and holding-period requirements, and test principal-purpose and anti-abuse provisions. Apply the reduced rate only where French procedural requirements permit relief at source; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund using the applicable French forms and supporting residence documentation. Maintain board resolutions, shareholder registers, payment records, treaty forms, residence certificates, and evidence that the recipient is not an artificial conduit. Treaty relief must be reassessed for each material change in ownership, residence, or beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on certain French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty reductions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to accounts or persons in non-cooperative jurisdictions and anti-abuse or recharacterization cases. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to approximately 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, recipient status, and limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions. EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief may apply to qualifying associated companies subject to ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million of French turnover or gross assets, or membership in a group meeting the EUR 400 million threshold, generally triggers full Local File and Master File documentation obligations under French transfer-pricing rules. A French transfer-pricing summary declaration on Form 2257-SD generally applies at a lower EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where the relevant group threshold is met. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single stand-alone economic-substance regulation equivalent to a comprehensive offshore ESR regime. Substance is enforced through the French anti-abuse doctrine, abuse-of-law rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, treaty principal-purpose tests, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and general arm's-length principles. A French SAS must maintain real business functions, appropriate personnel or outsourced operational control, decision-making evidence, commercially justified contracts, accounting records, and risk-bearing capacity. An affiliate media-buying company should demonstrate genuine campaign management, platform relationships, lead-generation activity, pricing control, fraud monitoring, and performance risk rather than acting as a conduit for foreign profits.
industry_specific_transfer_pricing_contr: Affiliate advertising commissions must be supported by measurable services, campaign records, conversion data, attribution methodology, cancellation and fraud policies, and economically rational margins.
Media purchases from related parties require evidence of platform access, inventory acquisition, rebates, credits, volume discounts, and allocation of media-buying risks.
Year-end management-fee or commission true-ups must be contractually authorized, consistently applied, and supported by contemporaneous calculations.
Payments to low-tax or no-tax affiliates require enhanced beneficial-ownership, substance, service-delivery, and commercial-purpose evidence.

French tax authorities may reject deductions where the recipient did not perform the invoiced services, where the charge is duplicative, or where the arrangement transfers profits without corresponding functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating advertising revenue, concealing affiliate commissions, using undisclosed payment accounts, fabricating invoices, or intentionally omitting taxable transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties of up to 80% of the avoided tax in aggravated cases, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000. Aggravated or organized conduct may attract imprisonment of up to seven years and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability and personal tax liability in cases of fraudulent maneuvering or serious and repeated non-compliance. Civil veil piercing is exceptional and is not automatic. Courts may impose confiscation, professional prohibitions, asset restraints, and travel restrictions where legally ordered; imprisonment is possible for qualifying criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing profits through a foreign affiliate with no personnel, decision-making, operational capability, or genuine service delivery; paying invoices for nonexistent media-buying, consulting, or lead-generation services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Expense denial, taxable-profit reassessment, withholding-tax assessment, abuse-of-law penalties, interest, and potentially fraud or false-accounting prosecution. A foreign company is not unlawful merely because it is low-substance; the risk arises from fictitious, abusive, or misrepresented transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly approve fictitious transactions, false books, or fraudulent tax structures. Asset confiscation, management bans, and imprisonment may apply under the underlying offense; travel restrictions require a specific judicial or administrative basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying non-arm's-length commissions, shifting residual profit to a foreign affiliate without corresponding functions and risks, failing to document controlled transactions, or using unsupported year-end adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the arm's-length principle, denial of deductions, withholding-tax consequences, interest, and documentation penalties. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can generally trigger the higher of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions lacking documentation, subject to the applicable statutory cap and rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for deliberate falsification or fraudulent concealment, but ordinary transfer-pricing disagreement normally creates corporate tax liability rather than automatic director imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming input VAT on fictitious media invoices, misclassifying cross-border digital services, failing to reverse-charge imported services, or using false customer or supplier identities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, recovery of improperly claimed credits, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% for serious non-compliance to 80% for fraudulent or concealed conduct, and possible criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be prosecuted for intentional VAT fraud or knowingly false records. Corporate fines, confiscation, professional bans, and imprisonment may apply under the relevant criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying treaty relief without a valid tax-residence certificate, paying dividends, royalties, or commissions to a conduit, or failing to withhold on a payment subject to French domestic withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, interest, penalties, denial of treaty benefits, and possible joint or secondary liability under applicable tax rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise where directors knowingly authorize non-compliant payments or fraudulent treaty claims. Good-faith reliance on properly documented treaty relief does not eliminate the need for reasonable verification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Mercury, Wise, ACH, or wire transfers to layer proceeds, conceal beneficial owners, process unexplained third-party funds, or make payments inconsistent with invoices and commercial contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting, account restriction or closure, asset freezing, forfeiture, and money-laundering prosecution. Money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 375,000; aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of up to ten years and a fine of up to EUR 750,000, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and beneficial owners may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, facilitation, or concealment. Corporate criminal fines may be up to five times the individual fine where applicable, with confiscation and management prohibitions possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, backdating contracts, manipulating conversion or attribution data, recording personal expenses as media costs, or creating false invoices and board records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting corrections, tax reassessment, corporate-law penalties, civil damages, and criminal sanctions for document fraud, false records, or distribution of fictitious dividends, depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, directors, de facto managers, accountants, and approving officers may incur individual civil and criminal liability. Corporate limited liability does not protect a person from liability for personal fraud or intentional misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Profit Distribution and Insolvency Misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, extracting funds through disguised shareholder loans, continuing distributions while insolvent, or preferring related-party creditors before insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, shareholder and director claims, insolvency clawback, asset recovery, management liability, and possible criminal sanctions for fictitious dividends or bankruptcy-related misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to insolvency shortfalls where management faults caused or increased the deficiency and may face management bans, asset confiscation, or imprisonment for qualifying insolvency offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to disclose sponsored affiliate relationships, using misleading performance claims, generating invalid leads, manipulating clicks or conversions, or processing personal data unlawfully in advertising campaigns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines, consumer compensation, platform clawbacks, contract termination, administrative sanctions, and potential GDPR penalties of up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for intentional deceptive practices, obstruction, or criminal data offenses. Corporate limited liability does not shield individuals from their own unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Corporate and Tax Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SAS solely as a pass-through entity, making strategic decisions outside France while claiming French functions, lacking personnel or controlled outsourcing, or having no evidence of campaign execution and risk assumption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, reallocation of profits, treaty-benefit denial, permanent-establishment disputes, tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and possible abuse-of-law treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for deliberate misrepresentation or fraudulent arrangements. A lack of substance alone does not automatically create imprisonment or veil piercing, but it materially increases audit, reassessment, and anti-abuse exposure.
